name: Variegated Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of northern colombia to western venezuela, eastern ecuador, and southern peru
description: Small flycatcher found in foothill and subtropical forest from around 1500-2300m. Grizzled face pattern with bold black and white crescent on cheek like some other bristle-tyrants and tyrannulets.

name: Schneider's Pitta
rangeDescription: Primary forest of montane sumatra
description: Large-headed and long-legged, this rare and rotund Sumatran endemic is found only in foothill forests between 900 to 2400 meters (typically in the upper half), where it is most easily detected by its strange song, a spaceship-like “oowOOOOwooWOOH.” Male has a sky-blue back and incomplete black collar, while the female has a dull brownish back and a dull blue tail. Both sexes have a rich cinnamon crown and nape, as well as a dark line extending behind the eye.

name: Rough-legged Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of eastern bolivia, northern argentina, eastern paraguay, and southeastern brazil
description: Small flycatcher found in forest canopy. Confusingly similar to other tyrannulets, but note especially its stubby (not pointy) bill with a very pale base, which can be quite evident since you are often looking straight up at the bird.

name: Sichuan Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Breeds in southern china (shaanxi, sichuan, guizhou, hubei, northwestern hunan, and northwestern jiangxi); nonbreeding range unknown
description: Drab brown warbler of hilly central China; russet-brown above and cold gray-brown below, with dark stripes on the vent. Like many other bush warblers, very difficult to see as it skulks deep in dense vegetation; typically prefers to scurry or run instead of fly to reach cover.

name: Buff-bridled Inca-Finch
rangeDescription: Arid andes of western peru (upper marañón valley drainage)
description: Perhaps the most beautiful of the five species of inca-finch; restricted to the upper parts of the Marañon Valley and its tributaries in the Andes of northern Peru. It has a yellow bill and legs, a black face and throat, and a chestnut back; its buffy belly and mustache set it apart from all the other inca-finches.

name: Hill Swallow
rangeDescription: Southern india and sri lanka
description: A small dark blue-black swallow with rufous-chestnut on its face and a short tail. Except for a black triangular eye-stripe extending to the bill, the entire forehead, chin, throat, and upper breast are rufous-chestnut, without any dark necklace like that of Barn Swallow, the main confusion species.

name: Crested Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Montane forest of jamaica
description: A plump dove that inhabits dense, moist forests in foothills and mountains. Prefers dense leaf litter, but is sometimes found along trails and roadsides.

name: Kilombero Weaver
rangeDescription: Southeastern tanzania (floodplain of kilombero river)
description: A fairly small and slim weaver with a relatively slender bill. Breeding male is distinctive, with bright yellow overall plumage and a black-and-chestnut bib.

name: Green Aracari
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela to the guianas and northern brazil
description: Common small toucan of rainforest canopy. The key field mark is the clear yellow belly that contrasts sharply with a dark breast.

name: Peruvian Wren
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of peru (amazonas to ayacucho)
description: An accomplished songster found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru. Some birds are almost entirely brown with faint black barring on wings and tail.

name: Small Ground-Finch
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of main galapagos islands
description: A small, widespread Galápagos finch. Bill is longer than it is deep, appears somewhat pointed, and has only a slight curve to the upper edge.

name: Pictorella Munia
rangeDescription: Northern australia (fitzroy river, western australia to northwestern queensland)
description: Small, grayish-brown bird with a scaly white bib, a dark black facial mask, buffy belly, and a gray bill. Juveniles very plain brown, with faint outline of adult's mask.

name: Santa Marta Wren
rangeDescription: High grassland of santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Highly endangered wren restricted to grassy and scrubby areas above tree line high up in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Reaching its habitat involves a multi-day camping expedition, and it cannot be seen in the commonly birded areas lower down the mountains.

name: Yellow-throated Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern assam (manipur and lushai hills) to western myanmar
description: A small, slim laughingthrush with an obvious yellow belly and black mask. Similar to Rufous-vented Laughingthrush, but the Yellow-throated Laughingthrush is smaller, with a smaller bill and a whitish vent and undertail.

name: Tepui Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela, southern guyana, and far northern brazil
description: The most numerous small parrot in the tepui highlands. Plumage entirely green with somewhat darker wings and a distinctive pale crescent below eye.

name: Jamaican Vireo
rangeDescription: Lowlands and mountains of jamaica
description: A small inhabitant of thickets in woodlands and scrublands where it feeds by actively searching for insects within tangles; avoids mangroves and well-manicured woodlands that lack dense undergrowth. The Greater Antillean Elaenia shares this species’ wingbars and overall dull coloration, but the elaenia has prominent whitish markings around the eye and is usually found perched upright or flycatching.

name: Pygmy Batis
rangeDescription: Arid southern ethiopia, sudan, somalia, and kenya to far northeastern tanzania
description: A small batis with typical black, white, and gray markings. Note the chest band, which is black in males and rufous in females.

name: White-breasted Babbler
rangeDescription: Locally in forest of western java
description: Rather chunky babbler with a gray head, snowy-white underparts, and bright rufous wings and tail. Endemic to Java, where it is quite local in forested lowlands and foothills.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Bushy-crested Hornbill
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar, malay peninsula, sumatra, borneo, and penang island
description: Plain, medium-sized dark hornbill. Glossy black with a bicolored tail and pale patches of bare facial skin.

name: Black-banded Barbet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of java and bali
description: Large barbet with an immense chisel-like bill. Leaf-green overall, with a red throat, black mask, and bright yellow crown and round spot at the base of the bill.
